Dante Alighieri, The Divine Comedy, translated by Henry Wadsworth Longfellow.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/dante-alighieri/the-divine-comedy/henry-wadsworth-longfellow

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Dante Alighieri, the author, died 1321 (Wikidata Q1067, death date 1321-09-13).
- Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, the translator, died 1882 (Wikidata Q152513, death date 1882-03-24).

First publication of the text used: 1867 (the English translation; the Italian original was completed in 1320) (SE colophon: 'The Divine Comedy was completed in 1320 by Dante Alighieri. It was translated from Italian in 1867 by Henry Wadsworth Longfellow.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the edition's own statement of rights, quoted below, says the text is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin: every person named above died in 1925 or earlier (the last to die, Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, died in 1882), so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: the publication and translation years quoted above.
- Wikidata Q1067 (Dante Alighieri), death date 1321-09-13.
- Wikidata Q152513 (Henry Wadsworth Longfellow), death date 1882-03-24.
